meta.description: Thiago Cerqueira, founder of Teagar Company: custom software, APIs, integrations and AI-powered automation for businesses. Based in Brazil, working 100% remotely.
meta.ogDescription: Custom software, integrations and automation built to survive production.
meta.portraitAlt: Portrait of Thiago Cerqueira, with curly hair and a white t-shirt, lit in warm orange light

hero.lead: I'm Thiago Cerqueira, also known as Teagar. At Teagar Company I design and build web systems, integrations and AI-powered automation for businesses ready to replace spreadsheets, rework and manual processes with reliable software.

services.title: What Teagar Company delivers
services.intro: From diagnosis to deployment. Every delivery has a scope, acceptance criteria and evidence — not just a pretty screen.

items.title: Custom software
items.body: Web systems, internal portals and dashboards shaped around how your team actually works, with permissions, audit trails and clean data.

items.title: Process automation
items.body: Repetitive work, gone: data entry, reconciliations, notifications and reports that today depend on someone copying and pasting.

items.title: Integrations and APIs
items.body: Connecting ERPs, CRMs, payment providers, messaging and spreadsheets — with error handling, idempotency and logs.

items.title: Applied AI and agents
items.body: Assistants, MCP servers and multi-agent workflows wired into your systems, with clear limits on cost, access and privacy.

items.title: Websites and digital presence
items.body: Company sites, landing pages and showcases that are fast, accessible and bilingual, ready for search and for conversion.

items.title: Technical consulting
items.body: Bottleneck mapping, architecture reviews and an evolution plan for teams and companies that already run software.

work.title: Selected work
work.intro: Teagar Company's own products, systems in development and open-source projects. Some code is private; the thinking is here.

contrib.title: Open-source contributions
contrib.intro: My code, reviewed and merged by maintainers of other people's projects.
contrib.projectNote: A Wayland desktop shell with about 12k GitHub stars. Two of my plugins are part of its official community plugin repository.

items.name: OmniRoute Quota
items.summary: A bar widget and panel showing the remaining quota of every account configured in OmniRoute, with reset countdowns and seven-day local usage. The collector reads storage read-only and never exposes tokens to the UI.

items.name: Niri Workspace Preview
items.summary: An interactive widget that draws proportional maps of every Niri workspace from IPC metadata alone, preserving column and stack geometry, with per-monitor scoping.

items.name: Gartrol
items.summary: A local-first control plane for human and multi-agent work. Cards act as contracts (what, why and how to confirm), with claims, leases, evidence, auditable costs and model routing by complexity. This site was planned and delivered inside it.

items.name: Teagarden
items.summary: A desktop environment for multi-agent development: workspaces, paned terminals, missions and orchestration of coding agents, with session persistence and restore.

items.name: Egogero Condominium
items.summary: Pedestrian and vehicle access control for residential buildings through single-use, time-boxed invitations. Multi-tenant, role-based access (provider, manager, resident, front desk), OIDC with PKCE, MFA, outbox and immutable audit log.

items.name: Teagar showcases
items.summary: Two showcases built on the Teagar Company design system: an editorial fashion store and a responsive online menu. Static, accessible and published on GitHub Pages.

items.name: Crawl Online
items.summary: A cross-platform mod that adds native online multiplayer to Crawl with a host-authoritative model: every player runs and renders their own copy of the game, kept in sync over the network.

items.name: Craftônica: Robotics Lab
items.summary: An educational electronics mod for Minecraft: wires, power sources, resistors, LEDs and a multimeter as blocks, backed by a DC circuit solver that is independent from the game engine.

items.name: Multi-agent tutorials
items.summary: Two MVPs documented step by step — a ticket dashboard and a service monitor — built by coding agents working in parallel, with cards, tests, screenshots and handoffs.

items.name: Linux tooling
items.summary: Everyday utilities released as open source: a DaVinci Resolve video converter (on the AUR), a visual GPU profile switcher for Intel/NVIDIA laptops and a safe disk-space cleaner for Arch Linux.

items.name: Systems Programming track
items.summary: Open teaching material with 21 modules: logic, PHP, MySQL, HTML/CSS, JavaScript, REST APIs, MVC and Laravel. Each module has 20 progressive exercises, a capstone challenge and an answer key on a separate branch.

process.title: How a project moves
process.intro: No black box. You always know what is being built, why, and how to confirm it is done.

steps.title: Diagnosis
steps.body: A conversation to understand the process, the bottleneck and what success means for your business.

steps.title: Proposal
steps.body: Fixed scope, timeline, investment and written acceptance criteria — before a single line of code.

steps.title: Build
steps.body: Short, verifiable deliveries with demos, tests and a record of every decision.

steps.title: Operate
steps.body: Deployment, monitoring, documentation and support so the system keeps standing after handoff.

about.title: Software engineer, founder and teacher
paragraphs: I'm Thiago Cerqueira — Teagar online. I've been publishing open-source code since 2021 and turned that work into Teagar Company, a technology company focused on custom software, integrations and automation for businesses across Brazil and anywhere, working remotely.

My focus is back-end, real-time systems and applied AI. Today I build tools that coordinate coding agents with the same rigor as a human team: clear contracts, delivery evidence and costs under control.
I also teach. I maintain an open Systems Programming track and believe that explaining well is part of building well.
